% A test for tex8web: amsthm's \qedhere where the display has more of its
% own: a \label (also in \[ \]), a \tag, a nested environment, text; a
% second \qedhere or one outside a proof; and a proof that ends in a list.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{amsmath,amsthm}
\begin{document}
\begin{proof}[Label]
A.
\begin{equation}\label{eq:a} a = b \qedhere \end{equation}
\end{proof}
\begin{proof}[Tag]
A.
\begin{equation*} a = b \tag{x} \qedhere \end{equation*}
\end{proof}
\begin{proof}[Label align]
A.
\begin{align} a &= b \\ c &= d \label{eq:b} \qedhere \end{align}
\end{proof}
\begin{proof}[No tag align]
A.
\begin{align} a &= b \\ c &= d \notag \qedhere \end{align}
\end{proof}
\begin{proof}[Aligned]
A.
\[ \begin{aligned} a &= b \\ c &= d \qedhere \end{aligned} \]
\end{proof}
\begin{proof}[Text]
A.
\[ a = b \quad \text{done} \qedhere \]
\end{proof}
\begin{proof}[Twice]
A.
\[ a = b \qedhere \]
B.
\[ c = d \qedhere \]
\end{proof}
\begin{proof}[Bracket label]
A.
\[ a = b \label{eq:c} \qedhere \]
\end{proof}
Outside a proof, no box and no number lost:
\begin{align} a &= b \\ c &= d \qedhere \end{align}
\begin{equation}\label{eq:e} e = f \end{equation}
See \eqref{eq:a}, \eqref{eq:b} and \eqref{eq:e}. And \ref{eq:c}.
\begin{proof}[List]
\begin{itemize}\item One.\end{itemize}
\end{proof}
\end{document}
